title: Upright Row
summary: A barbell or cable pull up the front of the body for the side delts and upper traps.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar) or EZ curl bar; weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.8 for side delts (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly side delts total.
Library rating 0.8 for traps (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.3 for biceps (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly biceps total.

setup.text: Hold the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart, or wider.
Pull it up close to your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your elbows are about shoulder height.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar up close to your body
Stop when elbows reach shoulder height
A wider grip and stopping at shoulder height are the setup most lifters find comfortable.

mistakes.text: Using a very narrow grip and yanking the bar to the chin.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where a missed rep can be set down, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
